aspects.says: The setup is verified end to end by sending an 0800 network-management request and expecting an 0810 back.
aspects.reason: it needs a running server to answer, and a graded run is offline

aspects.says: Application code does not build the mux; it looks up the one Q2 deployed, by the name given in the mux's deploy file.
aspects.reason: standard jPOS convention (the mux looked up by its deploy name); general knowledge answers it without the page, so no quiz makes the page necessary (register ruling on ISO-M10/12)

aspects.says: The channel adaptor and the mux talk through named queues that cross: what the mux writes is what the channel sends, and what the channel receives is what the mux reads.
aspects.reason: standard jPOS convention (a channel adaptor's in/out queues crossed with the mux's); general knowledge answers it without the page, so no quiz makes the page necessary (register ruling on ISO-M10/12)

aspects.says: The client service sends a request through the mux and waits a bounded time for its answer.
basis: section:1.6 Creating a Simple ISO-8583 Client Service
aspects.reason: sending is page 4's subject and is practised there

aspects.says: Q2 and Spring run together: Q2 deploys the application as a QBean, and that QBean starts the Spring context from the application context file.
aspects.reason: configuration wiring, not an idea a reader is checked on
